notes: The Home Depot (homedepot.com). ACCESS: robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow. Homepage, sitemap XML files, and /daily-deals fetch cleanly via direct HTTP (curl_cffi, tier 1) and headless Playwright with a real Chrome fingerprint (tier 2); every /b/, /c/, and /s/ path returns a consistent Akamai-edge 403 under both tiers, matching the prior Home-Decor pass's finding. Did not escalate to Claude-in-Chrome (tier 3) since it requires interactive browser selection this synchronous worker cannot perform, and tier 1+2 already produced a well-supported, evidence-based absence answer (not an access failure) - see below. SALE VS CLEARANCE REASONING: (1) parsed the full current core-taxonomy sitemap (5,287 unfaceted category nodes) for Clearance/Outlet/Final-Sale/Last-Chance/End-of-Line/Discontinued keywords - zero hits; (2) sampled 6 of the 44 faceted PLP_REFINED sitemap shards (~270,000 URLs) for 'clearance'/'special-buy'/'sale'/'discount' - the only 2 literal 'clearance' hits are product-TYPE names, not merchandising concepts ('Zero-Clearance' electric-fireplace screens = a clearance-height product spec, and a 'Clearance Side Marker' towing light = a literal light-fixture name), so both are false positives, not a Clearance PLP; the ~99 'sale' hits sampled are all 'Labor-Day-Sale', a single named temporary seasonal campaign facet stacked on top of category pages, not a permanent clearance/outlet listing - excluded per the brief's Sale-vs-Clearance test (no permanence signal, it's a named calendar promotion); (3) the homepage 'Shop by Category' flyout (full list extracted) surfaces exactly 3 non-department tiles: 'Labor Day Savings' (temporary campaign, same as above), 'Daily Deals' (-> /daily-deals, opened directly: a rotating 'Deals of the Day' promo page built from themed shelves like 'Popular Picks'/'Top Rated', explicitly time-boxed, no permanence or outlet signal), and 'Special Savings' (-> /c/Savings_Center, a generic offers/specials hub - blocked 403 when fetched directly, but its own homepage label 'Special Savings' and its position alongside Daily Deals/Labor Day Savings in the same promo-tile row indicates it is a generic temporary-offers hub, not a dedicated Clearance/Outlet page); none of these three is described anywhere (breadcrumb, heading, on-page copy visible from the homepage tile data) as Clearance, Outlet, Final Sale, or End of Line. CONCLUSION: no genuine Clearance/Outlet-style PLP exists in Home Depot's current taxonomy or homepage-surfaced promotional shelving. Caveat: /b/ department pages themselves are blocked outright, so I could not directly load a department landing page to check for an in-department 'Clearance' facet/link that might not surface via sitemap URLs (facets are typically appended per-search, and my sitemap sampling covered only 6 of 44 shards for time) - flagging this residual gap rather than treating the finding as fully exhaustive.
